name: research retrospective after E11-E13
hypothesis: After 4 experiments (E11-E13 + first RETRO), re-examine patterns, Goodhart risks, and adversarial falsification to re-rank the experiment queue.
notes: 3 parallel independent subagents: (1) patterns — deterministic changes win, add-more-context regresses, measure-instrument-fix works; (2) Goodhart — coverage is mention-frequency proxy, hallucination is symbol-existence only, broken-examples 6.2% is largely self-inflicted via E13's <REQUIRED> placeholders (19 across 9/11 e2e pages, 10/13 residual findings), grounded-claims is a repetition-count; (3) adversarial — 7 source-verified factual errors in prose/tables, ALL missed by current checkers (method-vs-property confusion, return-type mismatches, arg-type mismatches, cross-page inconsistency). Key decisions: E13b (fix placeholder) promoted to NEXT; E18 (prose API semantics checker) promoted to second; E14 re-scoped with 2x-band threshold (4.2pp coverage, 24 grounded) and post-surgical placeholder-aware broken% as co-primary metric; add placeholder_value finding type to example_check.py; rename hallucination_rate to invented_symbol_rate. Synthesis at /tmp/rq-trials/agents/RETRO2_synthesis.md.

name: fix REQUIRED placeholder with value inference
hypothesis: Replacing E13's <REQUIRED> placeholder with a valid inferred value (from sibling kwargs or AST default) or omitting the kwarg with an annotation will make the broken-examples metric honest and eliminate the metric-gaming artifact.
changes: repoquill/surgical_verify.py: build_class_index now captures init_defaults (ast.unparse of default values); new _infer_value() function (Rule 1: AST default, Rule 2: judge_X mirrors X, Rule 3: provider mirrors judge_provider); _fix_missing_required_in_block uses _infer_value instead of inserting <REQUIRED>; _normalize_quotes for consistent double-quote style; trailing-comma detection to avoid double commas
/tmp/rq-trials/harness/example_check.py: new placeholder_value finding type; _is_placeholder() checks for <REQUIRED>, TODO, FIXME, PLACEHOLDER, ..., <value>, <arg>, <name> sentinel values
notes: BROKEN EXAMPLES: 13.8% mean (3 runs: 11.8, 21.2, 8.5) vs E13's 6.2%. The increase is HONEST — E13's <REQUIRED> placeholder satisfied the checker's missing_required test, hiding the true broken rate. E13b's inferred values are valid and runnable (e.g. judge_provider='ollama' when provider='ollama'). 0 placeholders across all 3 runs (vs 19 in E13). Remaining findings are missing_required (genuinely missing params the LLM didn't include) and occasional invalid_kwarg/syntax_error — these are GENERATION problems for E14 to address, not surgical verify problems. Coverage Run 1 (61.3%) is an outlier; Runs 2-3 (70.7%, 71.7%) are at or above baseline. Decision: KEEP — eliminates metric-gaming, coverage within 2x band, hallucination unchanged, grounded slightly higher.

hypothesis: Feeding prose-checker findings back into generation via targeted LLM correction reduces C-hallucination without coverage cost
design: E14 config + grounding_pass (new module: repoquill/grounding.py). 3 runs, each reuses E14_r{1,2,3} guides, runs prose checker, applies grounding pass, re-checks. Control: E14_r1-r3 (no grounding).
rationale: Prose findings dropped from 44.3 to 11.3 (74.5% reduction) with zero coverage loss (54.6% = 54.6%). Decision rule met: prose < 20 AND coverage >= 50.4%. Grounding pass is generic (works on any repo with prose-checker findings).

hypothesis: A semantic value checker that flags (a) string literal values in code blocks that are strict prefixes/abbreviations of the source parameter's default, and (b) method calls with known runtime caveats that are not mentioned in the page, will catch the 2 HIGH-severity C-hallucination errors identified by RETRO3 (language='en' vs 'English', missing event-loop RuntimeError caveat) without false positives.
experiment: Built eval/semantic_value_check.py with 2 checks: STRING_VALUE_MISMATCH (global param-name -> defaults map, prefix/abbreviation heuristic) and MISSING_CAVEAT (global method-name -> caveats map, key-phrase matching). Validated against E14 and E19 docs.
decision_rationale: Checker catches both known RETRO3 errors (3 language='en' mismatches + 9 missing event-loop caveats) with 0 false positives. Generic design (param-name-agnostic and method-name-agnostic) works for any repo. Confirms RETRO3 secondary check: grounding pass (E19) cannot fix these errors because they are outside the prose checker's finding types.
limitations: Prefix/abbreviation heuristic may miss non-prefix value errors (e.g. language='French' when default is 'English')
Caveat key-phrase list is fixed (event loop, RuntimeError, active event, thread, asyncio) — may miss other runtime condition patterns
Only checks fenced code blocks for string values, not inline code

hypothesis: Semantic value checker can catch C-hallucinations (string value mismatches, missing caveats) that other checkers miss
detail: EARLY VERSION: 20/23 false positives (provider='ollama', label_a='opus-4-7', etc. are legitimate user choices). The prefix/abbreviation heuristic was too aggressive — flagged any string value that was a prefix of the source default, including legitimate user-chosen values. SUPERSEDED by re-validation on 2026-08-29: current version of the checker correctly distinguishes user-chosen values from wrong defaults. Re-validated on E19_r3 docs: 11 findings (2 STRING_VALUE_MISMATCH for language='en', 9 MISSING_CAVEAT for event-loop restriction), 0 false positives. The 2 language='en' mismatches are genuine (source default is 'English'); all 9 MISSING_CAVEAT findings are genuine (no page mentions the event-loop restriction).

hypothesis: Wiring semantic checker into grounding pass enables LLM correction of semantic value errors
detail: grounding.py already consumed semantic_value_check findings alongside prose findings (wired in by RETRO3 subagents). _fix_page_grounding prompt includes instructions for STRING_VALUE_MISMATCH and MISSING_CAVEAT. No additional code change needed. E22 tests the combined grounding pass.

hypothesis: Feeding prose-checker findings back into generation via targeted LLM correction (grounding pass) will reduce prose API-semantics errors without degrading coverage or broken%
design: 3 runs. Each run: generate docs (E14 baseline config), run 4 checkers (pre), run grounding pass (feed prose findings + AST context to LLM for targeted correction), run 4 checkers (post). Decision: KEEP if prose findings drop >= 2x band (44.3 -> <20) AND coverage >= 50.4% (54.6% - 4.2pp band)
rationale: Prose findings: 43.3 -> 1.3 mean (97% reduction, far exceeds 2x band threshold of <20). Coverage unchanged (49.4% both pre and post). Broken% unchanged (10.5% both pre and post). Hallucination 0.0% in all runs. Grounding pass is deterministic in its input (prose findings + AST) and uses LLM only for targeted correction. The 10.5% broken% mean is higher than E14's 4.5% — this is generation variance (r2 had 21.1% broken), not a grounding-pass regression (broken% identical pre and post in all 3 runs).

hypothesis: Feeding the semantic value checker (E20) into the grounding pass will let the LLM correction pass fix string-literal mismatches (language='en' -> 'English') and add missing behavioral caveats (event-loop RuntimeError), closing the detect->fix->verify loop.
method: Extended repoquill/grounding.py to run BOTH prose_api_semantics_check.py AND semantic_value_check.py, merge findings, pass type-specific fix instructions to the LLM, re-run both checkers. Tested in isolation on E14 guides (OOM constraint blocks full generation).

summary: 5th experiment since RETRO3. Key findings: (1) E21 semantic reduction is real but tested in isolation (not full generation); (2) E21 coverage 56.4% is a single-run number at the top of the E14/E19 variance band, NOT a real improvement; (3) workflows category in coverage_check_v2.py is a Goodhart risk — admits generic English words as concepts, inflating denominator by ~14 false-positive concepts (~5pp coverage deflation); (4) no other Goodhart risks identified; (5) usability is the next blind spot — no metric measures whether docs are USEFUL to a new developer.

Do NOT claim E21 improved coverage (within variance band)
Establish 3-run mean for E21 best-known state

rationale: Coverage rose 2.1pp (below the conservative 3pp threshold), but the fix is valid: it removes 18 generic English words from the denominator, making the coverage metric more honest. The workflows category went from 50% to 55% documented. No other category affected. De-Goodhart fix per RETRO4.

hypothesis: The workflows category in coverage_check_v2.py admits generic English words (across, actually, around, etc.) as domain concepts via the frequency filter, inflating the denominator and deflating coverage by ~5pp (RETRO4 Goodhart risk).

hypothesis: Grounding pass variance (E22 showed inconsistent correction: r1 prose 32→2, r2/r3 prose 36→27/33→27) is caused by temperature 0.1 being too high or too many findings per page diluting the LLM's attention. Lowering temperature to 0.0 and/or capping findings at 5 will produce more consistent correction.
design: 4 variants × 3 runs: A (temp 0.1, max 20 = E19 config), B (temp 0.0, max 20), C (temp 0.1, max 5), D (temp 0.0, max 5). All prose-only grounding (no semantic checker).
rationale: No variant beats E19 on all metrics simultaneously. B (temp 0.0) has best prose (1.3) and coverage (55.1%) but broken 13.9% (E19: 5.2%). C/D (max 5) have terrible prose (21.7/22.7) — limiting findings makes the LLM fix fewer issues. A (same config as E19) has broken 9.1% vs E19's 5.2% — this is base-generation variance, not a grounding-pass effect. Key insight: dominant broken-example failure mode is syntax_error from API signature snippets (legitimate documentation pattern, not actually broken). This is a Goodharting concern: the metric counts signature snippets as 'broken' when they're not really broken. Code changes (grounding_temperature, grounding_max_findings, grounding_semantic config options) KEPT for future experiments.

hypothesis: Fixing the example checker to exclude API signature snippets (which are legitimate documentation, not executable code) will reduce the broken-examples rate without affecting generation quality.
changes: eval/example_check.py: added _is_signature_block() to detect and skip API signature snippets (Name(...) or Name.Name(...) patterns with type annotations that fail to parse as valid Python)
rationale: Checker fix is correct (properly excludes signature snippets — no syntax_error findings in E25 runs), but E25's broken% (13.5% mean) is WORSE than E19 (4.2% mean) with the same fixed checker. The high broken% is a real quality issue: the LLM is generating genuinely broken examples (property_called_as_method, missing_required, invalid_kwarg). The checker fix doesn't improve generation quality — it only makes the metric more honest. Coverage also regressed (51.2% vs 54.6%).
next: Investigate why E25 runs have more broken examples than E19. Possible causes: (1) grounding pass is introducing errors, (2) LLM variance, (3) config differences. Consider running E19 config without grounding pass to isolate the variable.

hypothesis: Running E19 config WITHOUT grounding pass will isolate whether the grounding pass introduces broken examples. If broken% drops significantly without grounding → grounding pass is the cause of E25's regression. If broken% is similar → LLM variance.
rationale: E26 (WITHOUT grounding) has broken% = 15.2% — WORSE than E25 (WITH grounding, 13.5%) and E19 (WITH grounding, 4.2%). The grounding pass is NOT the cause of the broken-example regression. The dominant error type is property_called_as_method (13/14 findings in r1) — the LLM consistently calls @property attributes as methods. Root cause: extract_api_surface() lists ALL FunctionDef items as 'methods' without checking for @property decorators, so the LLM sees score() in the API surface and correctly calls it as a method. E27 will fix this.
next: E27: Mark @property attributes in API surface extraction + add prompt rule.

hypothesis: Marking @property attributes as PROPERTIES (not methods) in the API surface extraction, plus adding a prompt rule to use them as attributes, will eliminate the dominant property_called_as_method broken-example type.
changes: repoquill/reference.py: extract_api_surface() now detects @property and @cached_property decorators, lists them separately as [PROPERTIES: name1, name2] instead of in the methods list
repoquill/narrative.py: Added rule 7 to strict prompt: PROPERTIES are attributes, NOT methods. Use them as obj.name, never as obj.name()
rationale: property_called_as_method = 0 in 3/3 runs (was the dominant error type in E25/E26). Broken% 3.5% (E19: 4.2%, E25: 13.5%, E26: 15.2%). Coverage 55.1% (E19: 54.6%, within 4.2pp band). Halluc 0.0% (E19: 0.3%). Remaining broken findings are syntax_error (5 total across 3 runs) from legitimate code blocks, not property calls. Generic fix — any Python package with @property benefits.
next: E28: Investigate remaining syntax_error findings (5 across 3 runs) or move to usability metric.

hypothesis: The 5 remaining syntax_error findings across E27 runs are from code blocks with leading indentation (a formatting artifact), not genuine code errors. Stripping leading indentation from code blocks before syntax-checking will eliminate the spurious findings.
changes: eval/example_check.py: extract_python_blocks() now applies textwrap.dedent() to each code block before returning it. This strips leading indentation that the LLM sometimes adds to the entire code block (including the fence), which causes a spurious "unexpected indent" syntax error at line 1.
rationale: De-Goodhart fix: the metric now measures code correctness, not markdown formatting. All 5 syntax_error findings were from indented code blocks (formatting artifact), not genuine code errors. The remaining 1 missing_required finding in E27_r2 is a genuine error (AuditExperiment() missing 'models' param). Broken% drops from 3.5% to 0.7% mean. No generation change — evaluation infrastructure only.
next: E29: Investigate the 1 remaining missing_required finding (AuditExperiment() missing 'models' param) or move to usability metric.

hypothesis: The 1 remaining missing_required finding in E27_r2 (AuditExperiment() missing 'models' param) is either a genuine generation error or a checker false positive.

results.analysis: models is a required param (no default) in AuditExperiment.__init__. The LLM generated AuditExperiment() without it in 1/9 cases (E27_r2 cli-reference.md). In the other 8 AuditExperiment() calls across 3 runs, the LLM correctly includes models. This is a one-off generation error, not a systematic issue.

rationale: The E14 constructor signature enrichment is working correctly (8/9 calls include required params). The 1 missing_required finding is within variance. No prompt change or checker refinement warranted for a single one-off error.
